name: Greimasian Brand Semiotic Square
diagnostic: What structural oppositions and contradictions define the narrative space of our category, and what unexplored territory can we claim?
artifact: A 4-Corner Structural Semiotic Matrix: Primary Assertion (S1) vs. Contrary (S2), and Contradictory (~ S1) vs. Sub-Contrary (~ S2), mapping category positions and white space.
trap: Positioning a brand on an unresolved contradictory axis without addressing the underlying semantic trade-offs.

origin.line: Algirdas Julien Greimas (1966), adapted by Jean-Marie Floch (1988)

pedigreeFull: Algirdas Julien Greimas (*Structural Semantics*, 1966) adapted to corporate semiotics by Jean-Marie Floch (1988). A logical tool that maps out the semantic limits and relationships of meaning within a category.

sourceNote: The source writes the four corners in escaped LaTeX (math-mode delimiters around S with subscript markers); the declared rendering table drops those delimiters, so the card prints S1, S2, ~S1, ~S2.
